analysis:
The two supplied units (CHANGELOG.md lines 1265-1709) are BASE-side historical changelog text. The only changed hunk in the patch excerpt (head lines 11-176, base 11-13) is not visible in these units, apart from a truncated head excerpt. I saw no executable code, configuration or policy in the supplied text. The base text is documentation of previously shipped behavior (Autopilot rewards, account erasure, App Attest/MDM freeze, SSD prefix cache, cache reliability, provider replacement). Nothing in it is changed by this PR, so I do not attribute pre-existing issues to it.

The PR's head hunk is a v0.10.5 candidate changelog entry. The truncated excerpt mentions MLX pin bumps (mlx, mlx-swift, mlx-swift-lm), a changed metallib hash, per-build SSD complete-checkpoint namespaces (binary and metallib hash binding, relevant to T-041 cache isolation), and a darkbloom sandbox CLI that runs an installer from api-sandbox.darkbloom.dev (relevant to TB-013/T-061/A-019, which already exist in the threat model). This is documentation only. The actual pin changes, kernel changes and installer code are not supplied here, so the security effect of the pins and the sandbox command cannot be assessed. No threat-model gap is evident, because TB-013/T-061 already cover the installer flow and T-041 covers the cache namespace.

Remaining integration questions: whether the actual code PR files (not in this batch) that change the pinned submodules, ProviderCore version and sandbox CLI preserve T-041 cache scoping and T-061 installer integrity controls. The changelog text alone gives no evidence of regression.
